summary: Negative GGUF rejection contract, source-read amplification measured by category, and an evaluation of the existing bounded authenticated range cache. Key results: a deterministic 14-case admission contract (2 accept incl. untied output, 12 safe rejections); the bounded 32 MB cache reduces disk read CALLS ~9.5x but not total source BYTES; and under SHA-256 authentication the cache is fully bypassed (re-read + re-hash), so integrity is never traded for throughput.

numerical_correctness_followup.task: Re-examine the Qwen teacher-forced top-1 flips beyond aggregate RMSE (prior session).
numerical_correctness_followup.method: Candidate-level comparison: resident top-1/top-2 tokens and logits, the reference margin, and the streamed logit at each candidate, from raw dumped f32 vectors (logit-diff --teacher-forced --dump-dir).
numerical_correctness_followup.result: Every flip is a near-tie: the streamed per-candidate error (0.05-0.17 at the flipped pair) exceeds a reference margin of 0.03-0.16, while non-flipping positions have margins 0.4-2.7 >> noise. Llama-3.2-1B is 16/16 EXACT (zero flips) and Stories110M is byte-exact, which a systematic attention/RoPE/FFN defect could not produce. Conclusion unchanged: permitted FP32 accumulation-order variance, no defect, no code or tolerance change. See qwen2_divergence_analysis_2026-11-23.json for the per-position margins.
numerical_correctness_followup.intermediate_tensor_taps: Not added. The final-logit candidate-margin analysis across three models (including one exact-agreement model) is conclusive; adding per-op FFI taps was judged unnecessary surface and is recorded as a scope decision, not a gap in the conclusion.

modern_rope_scaling_investigation.finding: The pinned llama.cpp conversion bakes the llama-3 'llama3' RoPE scaling into the rope_freqs.weight tensor at conversion time; real GGUFs (e.g. Llama-3.2-1B) carry the baked tensor, not runtime llama.rope.scaling.* metadata. Runtime-metadata scaling is therefore not implemented (it would be speculative without a real model that uses it).
modern_rope_scaling_investigation.safety: Models that DO carry runtime llama.rope.scaling.* keys are safely REJECTED by the architecture metadata allowlist (verified by the rope-scaling case in the rejection contract), so there is no silent wrong inference and no risk of double-applying scaling.
modern_rope_scaling_investigation.double_application_guard: A model presenting both a baked rope_freqs.weight and runtime scaling keys is rejected (the scaling keys fail the allowlist), so scaling cannot be applied twice.

gguf_rejection_contract.mechanism: builds minimal in-memory GGUF fixtures and drives the native Decoder via inspect_streamed_shape; all rejections return a typed error with no crash.

io_amplification.method: streamed --metrics, ctx 128, threads 2, max_tokens 8, cache off.

categories.initial_authentication: one-time whole-file SHA-256 pass when --sha256 is supplied (amortized; not in the per-token stream)
categories.per_token_weight_streaming: dominant cost: the full weight set is re-read every forward pass (no persistent weight residency); source_bytes ~= (prefill + generated) x model payload
categories.mutation_detection_rereads: the consume read and the integrity re-read of the same range are intra-pass and local; these are the repeated small ranges a tiny cache absorbs

bounded_cache_evaluation.implementation: existing CachedLocalReader (read_cache.rs); not re-implemented. No new cache added.
bounded_cache_evaluation.finding_calls_not_bytes: The 32 MB cache cuts disk read CALLS ~9.5x by absorbing immediate intra-pass re-requests of the same range, but total source BYTES are unchanged (the per-token working set is the whole model, which exceeds any bounded cache, so blocks evict before the next token re-reads them). Fewer read calls is NOT fewer physical bytes. A cache large enough to cut bytes would have to hold the whole model, contradicting out-of-core bounded memory.

security_authenticated_bypass.finding: Under authentication the LRU cache is fully bypassed (0 hits, 0 misses): each block is re-read and re-hashed (read_cache.rs:158, :496). For unauthenticated sources, cache hits revalidate source descriptor/path identity before publishing (read_cache.rs:148; tests cache_hit_rejects_changed_source_instead_of_serving_stale_weights, late_source_change_on_cache_hit_is_rejected_before_publication, authenticated_cache_hit_rejects_same_identity_in_place_rewrite). Integrity and mutation detection are NEVER weakened by the cache; the syscall benefit applies only to unauthenticated sources.

bounded_cache_evaluation.conclusion: The repository already provides a safe, bounded, authenticated range cache. It is a syscall-count optimization for unauthenticated sources, not a transfer-volume optimization, and it is correctly inert under authentication. No additional cache is justified; the synchronous re-read remains the integrity-preserving default for authenticated inference.
